modules.title: SQL Injection and Safe Querying
modules.goal: Treat every input as untrusted and keep SQL structure separate from data.

topics.title: Injection Basics
topics.simple: Injection input ko SQL code banata hai.
topics.pro: SQL injection happens when untrusted input is concatenated into a query and changes its structure.
points: Every database API is a boundary.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = 'Aarav' OR '1'='1';
example.output: The OR makes the predicate always true.

topics.title: String Concatenation
topics.simple: Input ko query string me jodna dangerous hai.
topics.pro: Concatenating user input into SQL lets quotes and operators escape the intended value.

example.sql: query = "SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = '" + input + "'";

topics.title: Prepared Statements
topics.simple: Prepared statements query structure fix karte hain.
topics.pro: A prepared statement parses the SQL once and supplies values separately, so input cannot change the structure.

example.sql:
PREPARE find_student (text) AS SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = $1;
EXECUTE find_student('Aarav');

topics.title: Parameterized Queries
topics.simple: Placeholders values ko safely bind karte hain.
topics.pro: Parameterized queries use $1, ? or named placeholders supplied by the driver, never string interpolation.

topics.title: ORM Safety
topics.simple: ORM raw fragments aur unsafe order clauses se bachna.
topics.pro: ORMs are safe for normal bound values but can expose injection through raw SQL, order-by strings and identifier interpolation.

topics.title: Identifier Quoting
topics.simple: Identifiers ko quote karo, values ko bind.
topics.pro: Identifiers cannot be parameterized like values; validate them against an allowlist and quote them correctly.
points: Do not quote values as identifiers.

topics.title: Dynamic SQL
topics.simple: Dynamic SQL identifiers ke liye allowlist use karo.
topics.pro: When a table or column must be dynamic, build it from a fixed allowlist and use format with %I for identifiers.

example.sql: EXECUTE format('SELECT * FROM %I WHERE id = $1', table_name) USING student_id;

topics.title: Input Validation
topics.simple: Validation format check karta hai, injection stop nahi karta.
topics.pro: Validation improves data quality but is not a substitute for parameterization because valid input can still contain SQL syntax.

topics.title: Least Privilege
topics.simple: Database role ko minimum rights do.
topics.pro: A compromised query can do less damage when the application role cannot drop tables or read unrelated schemas.

example.sql: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON students TO app_user;

topics.title: Error Leakage
topics.simple: Errors me schema details leak na karo.
topics.pro: Detailed database errors help attackers map tables and columns; return a generic message and log the detail server-side.

example.output: A message that should not reach the client.

topics.title: Stored Procedure Safety
topics.simple: Procedures bhi dynamic SQL se vulnerable ho sakti hain.
topics.pro: PL/pgSQL EXECUTE with concatenated input is injection-prone; use USING and format %I.

example.sql: EXECUTE format('SELECT * FROM %I WHERE id = $1', table_name) USING student_id;

topics.title: Escaping Is Not Enough
topics.simple: Manual escaping fragile hota hai.
topics.pro: Escaping depends on the database, encoding and context; parameterization removes the need to escape values at all.

topics.title: Second-Order Injection
topics.simple: Stored input baad me query me unsafe use ho sakta hai.
topics.pro: Second-order injection occurs when safely stored data is later concatenated into dynamic SQL without binding.

topics.title: Common Injection Patterns
topics.simple: OR 1=1, UNION aur comment tricks common hain.
topics.pro: Classic payloads alter predicates, append UNION queries or comment out the rest of the statement.

example.output: A payload that must remain data.

topics.title: Testing for Injection
topics.simple: Quotes, comments aur boolean payloads se test karo.
topics.pro: Security tests should confirm that quotes, UNION and time-based payloads are treated as literal data.

example.output: A query that treats the payload as text.

topics.title: Logging
topics.simple: Queries log karo but secrets redact karo.
topics.pro: Slow-query and audit logs help detect attacks, but they must not store passwords or tokens.

topics.title: WAF Is Not Enough
topics.simple: WAF layer help karta hai, root fix parameterization hai.
topics.pro: A web application firewall can block known payloads but cannot repair unsafe SQL or second-order paths.
points: Use WAF as defense in depth.

example.sql: -- Parameterize the query; the WAF is only an extra layer

topics.title: Safe Query Review
topics.simple: Review me string building aur dynamic SQL dhoondo.
topics.pro: A safe-query review looks for concatenation, raw SQL, dynamic identifiers and privileged roles.

topics.title: Safe JSON and Arrays
topics.simple: JSON input ko parse karo, SQL me string na jodo.
topics.pro: JSON and array inputs should be bound as values or parsed with typed functions, not interpolated into SQL.

topics.title: Practical Secure Query
topics.simple: Static SQL, bound values, allowlisted identifiers aur limited role.
topics.pro: A secure query keeps structure static, binds all data, validates identifiers against an allowlist and runs with least privilege.

example.sql: SELECT id, name FROM students WHERE email = $1;

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Injection Basics in a production query.
interview.answer: SQL injection happens when untrusted input is concatenated into a query and changes its structure. Key rules: Input must not become code. Parameters separate data. Every database API is a boundary.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain String Concatenation in a production query.
interview.answer: Concatenating user input into SQL lets quotes and operators escape the intended value. Key rules: Avoid building SQL with + or ||. Use placeholders. Never trust client validation.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Prepared Statements in a production query.
interview.answer: A prepared statement parses the SQL once and supplies values separately, so input cannot change the structure. Key rules: Parse first. Bind values later. Use the driver API.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Parameterized Queries in a production query.
interview.answer: Parameterized queries use $1, ? or named placeholders supplied by the driver, never string interpolation. Key rules: Use $1 in PostgreSQL. Bind every value. Do not concatenate identifiers.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain ORM Safety in a production query.
interview.answer: ORMs are safe for normal bound values but can expose injection through raw SQL, order-by strings and identifier interpolation. Key rules: Prefer the query builder. Bind raw fragments. Whitelist sort columns.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Identifier Quoting in a production query.
interview.answer: Identifiers cannot be parameterized like values; validate them against an allowlist and quote them correctly. Key rules: Use quote_ident in dynamic SQL. Allowlist table and column names. Do not quote values as identifiers.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Dynamic SQL in a production query.
interview.answer: When a table or column must be dynamic, build it from a fixed allowlist and use format with %I for identifiers. Key rules: Use format with %I. Allowlist names. Bind values separately.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Input Validation in a production query.
interview.answer: Validation improves data quality but is not a substitute for parameterization because valid input can still contain SQL syntax. Key rules: Validate type and length. Still bind values. Never rely on validation alone.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Least Privilege in a production query.
interview.answer: A compromised query can do less damage when the application role cannot drop tables or read unrelated schemas. Key rules: No superuser. Grant only needed tables. Separate admin access.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Error Leakage in a production query.
interview.answer: Detailed database errors help attackers map tables and columns; return a generic message and log the detail server-side. Key rules: Log internally. Show generic errors. Do not echo SQL.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Stored Procedure Safety in a production query.
interview.answer: PL/pgSQL EXECUTE with concatenated input is injection-prone; use USING and format %I. Key rules: Bind with USING. Quote identifiers with %I. Validate allowlists.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Escaping Is Not Enough in a production query.
interview.answer: Escaping depends on the database, encoding and context; parameterization removes the need to escape values at all. Key rules: Do not hand-roll escaping. Use driver parameters. Keep SQL structure static.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Second-Order Injection in a production query.
interview.answer: Second-order injection occurs when safely stored data is later concatenated into dynamic SQL without binding. Key rules: Treat stored data as untrusted. Bind on every use. Audit dynamic reporting tools.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Common Injection Patterns in a production query.
interview.answer: Classic payloads alter predicates, append UNION queries or comment out the rest of the statement. Key rules: Never concatenate. Test with quotes and operators. Use allowlists.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Testing for Injection in a production query.
interview.answer: Security tests should confirm that quotes, UNION and time-based payloads are treated as literal data. Key rules: Test quote handling. Test UNION. Test boolean and time payloads.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Logging in a production query.
interview.answer: Slow-query and audit logs help detect attacks, but they must not store passwords or tokens. Key rules: Log parameters carefully. Redact secrets. Alert on patterns.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain WAF Is Not Enough in a production query.
interview.answer: A web application firewall can block known payloads but cannot repair unsafe SQL or second-order paths. Key rules: Use WAF as defense in depth. Fix the query. Do not rely on signatures.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Safe Query Review in a production query.
interview.answer: A safe-query review looks for concatenation, raw SQL, dynamic identifiers and privileged roles. Key rules: Search for string building. Check raw ORM calls. Verify allowlists.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Safe JSON and Arrays in a production query.
interview.answer: JSON and array inputs should be bound as values or parsed with typed functions, not interpolated into SQL. Key rules: Bind JSON as a parameter. Use jsonb operators. Validate shape.

interview.q: Module 30 · Explain Practical Secure Query in a production query.
interview.answer: A secure query keeps structure static, binds all data, validates identifiers against an allowlist and runs with least privilege. Key rules: Static structure. Bound values. Allowlisted identifiers. Least privilege.

debug.title: Classic concatenation
debug.broken: query = "SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = '" + name + "'";
debug.fix: query = "SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = $1"; values = [name];
debug.error: The input can change the predicate

debug.title: UNION payload
debug.broken: input = "' UNION SELECT password FROM users --";
debug.fix: Bind input as a value; never concatenate it into SQL.
debug.error: The attacker appends a second result set

debug.title: ORDER BY injection
debug.broken: query = "SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY " + sort;
debug.fix: Allowlist sort columns and use quote_ident, e.g. ORDER BY id.
debug.error: ORDER BY cannot be a bound value

debug.title: Table name injection
debug.fix: Allowlist the table name and quote it with format('%I', table).
debug.error: The table name changes the statement

debug.title: Escaping alone
debug.broken: query = "SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = '" + input.replace(/'/g, "''") + "'";
debug.fix: Use a parameter instead of manual escaping.
debug.error: Encoding and context can defeat the escape

debug.title: Error leak
debug.broken: Return the raw PostgreSQL error to the browser.
debug.fix: Log the error server-side and return a generic message.
debug.error: The schema and SQL are exposed

debug.title: Procedure concatenation
debug.broken: EXECUTE 'SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = ' || student_id;
debug.fix: EXECUTE 'SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = $1' USING student_id;

debug.title: Second-order injection
debug.broken: SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = '" || stored_name || "'";

debug.title: Overprivileged app
debug.broken: GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_user;
debug.fix: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON students TO app_user;
debug.error: A compromised query can touch every table

debug.title: Dynamic identifier unquoted
debug.error: A crafted identifier breaks the statement
